lead.headline: Iran hits U.S. bases in Kuwait and UAE as Trump vows more strikes
lead.dek: Iran puts its toll from this week's U.S. strikes at 18 dead; Tehran says it laid new mines south of Hormuz.
body: Iran's army said Thursday it struck U.S. communications systems, depots and aircraft hangars at Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait and radar at Al Minhad Air Base in the United Arab Emirates with missiles and drones. Kuwait's army said its air defenses were engaging the attack, and its foreign ministry called it a flagrant violation of sovereignty. Neither country reported casualties.

Iran's health minister put the toll from this week's U.S. strikes at 18 dead and at least 108 wounded, and the Iranian Red Crescent asked the International Criminal Court to investigate the strike on a wedding in Kuhestak. Central Command said it does not target civilians and is looking into the reports; it said Wednesday's strikes hit air defenses, radar and mine-laying capability.

Trump called it "a very heavy attack" and said the U.S. is prepared to strike again "anytime we want"; Secretary of State Rubio said the June memorandum with Iran has essentially ended. An Iranian military spokesman said more mines were laid south of the Strait of Hormuz overnight, waters Central Command had declared cleared. Brent traded near $95.

briefs.headline: Edouard's remnants drop up to 21 inches on East Texas
briefs.summary: Flash flood emergencies covered parts of Hardin and Tyler counties Wednesday as 10 to 21 inches fell; deputies pulled a woman and four children from a Livingston mobile home, and 76,000 customers lost power.

briefs.headline: Judge refuses to break up Google's ad business
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema rejected the Justice Department's bid to force a sale of the AdX exchange Wednesday and ordered conduct remedies instead; her opinion stays sealed for 14 days.

briefs.headline: Beige Book finds modest growth, data centers driving demand
briefs.summary: The Fed's survey released Wednesday said activity rose modestly since early July in 10 of 12 districts, employment barely rose, and eight districts reported moderate price increases tied to energy costs.

briefs.headline: Maduro asks a New York judge to toss his drug indictment
briefs.summary: Lawyers for Nicolas Maduro and Cilia Flores argued Wednesday that head-of-state immunity bars the cocaine-trafficking case; Judge Alvin Hellerstein set arguments for Nov. 17, with trial set for June 2027.

briefs.headline: Nepal's flood toll climbs to 1,252 with 4,216 still missing
briefs.summary: The disaster authority's count as of Thursday noon rose from 1,127 a day earlier; only 95 bodies have been identified, and about 900 hydropower workers are among the unaccounted for.

briefs.headline: Maltese jury acquits tycoon in Caruana Galizia murder
briefs.summary: A court cleared Yorgen Fenech Wednesday of orchestrating the 2017 car bombing that killed journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia; five others are already convicted, and her son called it a verdict "our country may never recover from."

briefs.headline: Pacific leaders split over rebuking China's missile test
briefs.summary: Australia and Palau are pressing the Pacific Islands Forum, closing its Palau retreat Thursday, to condemn July's ballistic missile test that flew more than 7,000 km to land near Tuvalu; Kiribati and Nauru object.

briefs.headline: Nigeria confirms the U.S. troops sent in February will leave
briefs.summary: Military spokesman Samaila Uba said the roughly 200 Americans deployed for training, intelligence and counterterrorism will withdraw, and the relationship "remains strong, enduring, and mutually beneficial." No date was given.

briefs.headline: Justice Wooton hospitalized after a medical incident on the bench
briefs.summary: Justice Bill Wooton was taken to a hospital during Wednesday morning's arguments, the first day of a fall term of more than 40 cases; court spokesman Jared Hunt said he was conscious and alert, and the rest of the day's arguments were canceled.

briefs.headline: Google-backed $350M solar plant planned for a Cannelton mine site
briefs.summary: MN8 Energy and Google announced the Mammoth Solar project Wednesday on a reclaimed Kanawha County mine, with construction starting in 2027; the companies say it pairs 86 MW of solar with 80 MW of storage and about 200 construction jobs.

briefs.headline: State orders flat FY28 budgets despite a $46M revenue beat
briefs.summary: General revenue ran $46.1M above estimate through August, at $838.3M, but Revenue Secretary Eric Nelson has told agencies to hold requests at or below this year's levels and said the income-tax cut trigger will not be met.

briefs.headline: Black Diamond Power's sale window closes with no deal
briefs.summary: A PSC-ordered three-month period for the Sophia utility to negotiate a sale to Appalachian Power expired without an agreement, WVVA reported; it serves about 5,000 customers, and a status hearing is set for Sept. 21.

regional.item: Huntington will reinspect the six vacated houses near Marshall, three of them fraternity houses, starting next week, building inspector Todd Darst said Wednesday.
Putnam's delegates asked the governor and DOT for an expedited safety review of five U.S. 35 intersections after Friday's fatal crash; a consultant is under contract with no start date.
Parkersburg council voted 6-3 on first reading for a flat $3 monthly recycling fee on every household after a judge ruled the opt-in system violated state law.
Homer Hickam and the Rocket Boys come to Pipestem Resort State Park Friday at 4 p.m. for teacher Frieda Riley's induction into the West Virginia Hall of Fame.

away.item: VTrans finished the Bennington Bridge #6 replacement over the Walloomsac on Tuesday, five months after work began in April; only landscaping and cleanup remain.

hotspots.item: The Holly River State Park Festival runs Saturday and Sunday, Sept. 5-6, at Hacker Valley with a car show, craft vendors, live music and the Holly River Hustle 5K.
Pender's planning board voted 3-2 this week to recommend denying 930 age-55-plus homes on 404 acres off Sidbury Road near Hampstead; commissioners vote by mid-October.

briefs.headline: RCMP now call a missing Prince George man's death a homicide
briefs.summary: Julian Wich, 29, was last seen Dec. 10 and reported missing Jan. 2; his remains were found in the Fraser River June 19, and the Serious Crime Unit is asking for tips, Cpl. Jennifer Cooper said Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Former mayor Lyn Hall named chair of Northern Health
briefs.summary: Health Minister Ravi Kahlon appointed Hall, on the board since May 2025, to a term running to April 2029; Colleen Nyce steps down after nine years and moves to the Provincial Health Services board.

briefs.headline: Two more MLAs quit B.C. Conservatives; Findlay's chief of staff resigns
briefs.summary: Scott McInnes and Donegal Wilson became the eighth and ninth MLAs to leave the caucus since Aug. 14, both citing the leader's reported Alberta-separatist ties; Chris Delaney resigned hours later.

briefs.headline: Ottawa extends the gas-tax holiday to Jan. 31 at a $2.9B cost
briefs.summary: Finance Minister Champagne said Wednesday the 10-cent gasoline and 4-cent diesel excise pause, due to end at Labour Day, runs into 2027 and phases back in by April 1; the total cost is now $5.3B.

briefs.headline: Hubble finds a 10-sided jet stream over Saturn's south pole
briefs.summary: A decagon-shaped wave circling the pole is the first large regular-sided pattern seen in Saturn's southern hemisphere, a counterpart to the northern hexagon, a Basque Country-led team reports in Science Advances.

briefs.headline: Leukemia drug shrinks HIV's hidden reservoir in monkeys
briefs.summary: Emory researchers report in Nature Microbiology that 10 days of venetoclax with antiretroviral therapy cut infected cells in rhesus macaques faster than the therapy alone; two human trials are underway.

briefs.headline: Galaxies keep their hydrogen but stop making stars
briefs.summary: A survey of about 2.5 million galaxies with China's FAST telescope and DESI finds star formation was 2.5 times higher 4.5 billion years ago while neutral hydrogen was only 1.4 times higher, in Nature Astronomy.

briefs.headline: Alzheimer's-driving T cells are switched on outside the brain
briefs.summary: Washington University researchers found the CD8 cells that worsen tau damage are activated by dendritic cells in lymph nodes; removing those cells spared mice's brains and memory, in Nature Neuroscience.

briefs.headline: OpenAI rates its Astra model 'critical' for hacking ability
briefs.summary: The company said Astra posted a perfect ExploitBench score and found two zero-day flaws on its own, the first model to cross the top cyber tier of its Preparedness Framework; the claims have no outside verification.

briefs.headline: Justice Department backs OpenAI's fair-use defense against the Times
briefs.summary: A 20-page statement of interest in the Southern District of New York says constraining model training "under a misunderstanding of fair use doctrine would thwart such creative and scientific progress."

briefs.headline: 30 more lawsuits over the Tumbler Ridge shooting name OpenAI
briefs.summary: Teachers, a principal and students filed in California Wednesday, bringing the claims to 37 and adding a count of aiding and abetting the Feb. 10 attack that killed eight; OpenAI called an allegation that it withheld contact with police "absolutely false."
